headline: Gut microbial variants and databases link microbiome features to host disease
label: Gut Microbiome Host Association
summary: Large cohorts and curated resources now test gut microbial SNVs against host phenotypes at scale, yielding reusable association catalogues.
synthesis: The common thread is linking gut microbial features to host phenotypes and disease, with emphasis on reusable public resources. A microbiome-wide PheWAS tested 12.8M gut microbial SNVs against 244 host phenotypes in 10,781 people, reporting 940 associations and releasing a public summary-statistics catalogue. A structural equation framework integrates large microbiome cohorts with smaller paired microbiome-metabolome data to construct microbiome-metabolome-disease pathways. GutBiomeDB consolidates 168 464 human gut microbiome samples, and gutDBase integrates transcriptomic and microbial data from 175 bulk and single-cell datasets across 15 gut-related diseases. The new element is variant-level association at cohort scale, paired with cross-dataset integration, rather than a single shared method.
